newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Chretien formally calls June 2 election.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien formally calls June 2 election.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien on Sunday formally called a June 2 general election, 17 months before the required date, to try to capitalise on his large lead in the polls.

"I have just met with the Governor General, who has issued a writ dissolving Parliament. A general election will be held on June 2," he said. The governor-general is the representative of Canada's head of state, Queen Elizabeth.
"I will be asking Canadians to give the Liberal Party a new mandate to build on the record of the last four years," Chretien said in the prepared text.

Chretien, 63, has only governed for 3-1/2 years, but he has a broad lead in the polls over a badly split opposition that would help his party sweep to another election victory if voting trends hold until election day.
Chretien tried to show that relief was ahead after the tough deficit slashing his government implemented. "Today we see that the light at the end of the tunnel is growing brighter," he said.

But he refused to yield to calls for tax cuts being issued by the Conservative and Reform parties on his right, saying it would risk all the gains Canada had made "to introduce a tax cut before the country can afford one."
